fields.description:
ADP is a general-purpose platform. A repository it is piloted against must not appear in its committed configuration, and no tracked file should carry one developer's machine layout. This ticket closes both gaps and adds coverage so neither can reappear unnoticed.

The client repository reached tracked configuration through the compose override, which mounted it into the activity worker and, read-only, into the repository-intelligence services, and registered it in two `REPO_INTELLIGENCE_REPOS` values. Those entries sat beside the platform's own `agentic-demo-*` mounts, which belong there, so removal has to be surgical.

The operator's checks config was the one file in `config/local` that shipped a `.yaml.example` template without a matching ignore rule, so it was committed while `github`, `jira`, `integrations`, `gates`, `gate_engine`, `tickets`, and `review-trust-root` were not. The operator's copy carried a client entry and was held back only by a `skip-worktree` bit, which also hides local edits from `git status`. Bringing the file under the existing convention is the fix. No new mechanism is needed.

Project compose overlays had no ignore rule. The pilot overlay was excluded through `.git/info/exclude`, which protects one checkout and does not survive a fresh clone. A generic pattern with negations for the platform's own compose files closes this without naming any project.

Developer machine paths reached tracked files in three places. The documented base branch example used a personal account with a client ticket key, and the assertion that preserves that string verbatim used the same value. Every scorecard under the repository-intelligence eval directory recorded its gold set and its binary as absolute paths from whichever machine produced it. The harness that writes those records emitted the absolute path it was given and defaulted its corpus and binary to one maintainer's directory layout, so regenerating any scorecard reintroduced the leak. Normalising the records without changing the harness would leave the source of the leak in place.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No tracked file names the client repository, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_repo_hygiene.py -k no_tracked_file_names_a_client_repository`
- [ ] No tracked file carries a developer machine path, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_repo_hygiene.py -k no_tracked_file_carries_a_personal_account_path`
- [ ] Every scorecard records its provenance as a repository-relative path, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_repo_hygiene.py -k scorecard_provenance_paths_are_repository_relative`
- [ ] Every operator-edited config that ships an example is ignored, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_repo_hygiene.py -k every_operator_config_is_ignored_and_has_an_example`
- [ ] A project compose overlay is ignored, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_repo_hygiene.py -k project_compose_overlays_are_ignored`
- [ ] The platform's own compose files stay tracked, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_repo_hygiene.py -k the_platform_compose_files_stay_tracked`
- [ ] The documented base branch example uses a neutral account, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_intake_base.py -k slashed_branch_is_preserved`

## Testing
Run each acceptance criterion selector on its own. Run `PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/inv ci` before closing the ticket.
